name: Typha
look_here_first: Confirm the upper staminate and lower pistillate spike zones. On an intact flowering stem, measure the naked gap; then check the inner sheath and first 1–10 cm of the leaf blade for glands. Confirm bracteoles and stigma shape under magnification when characters conflict.
shared_genus_traits: Rhizomatous marsh herbs with long linear leaves.
Upper staminate and lower pistillate cylindrical spike zones.

species_comparison_matrix.latifolia: Usually contiguous, but some clones can show a gap up to 4 cm (rarely 8 cm).

species_comparison_matrix.domingensis: Fresh widest blades usually 6–18 mm (FNA); ranges overlap.
species_comparison_matrix.latifolia: Fresh widest blades usually 10–23 mm, occasionally to 29 mm (FNA); ranges overlap.

species_comparison_matrix.caution: Overlap at 24–25 mm; measure mature spikes.

cautions: Hybridization, spike damage and leaf plasticity make any single character unreliable.
Technical bracteole/gland confirmation belongs to diagnostic review.
FNA documents naked-axis gaps even in some T. latifolia clones; a visible gap is suggestive, not proof of T. domingensis.
lookalikes: Schoenoplectus: branched sedge spikelets, not two vertically separated cattail spike zones.
diagnostic_photo_checklist: Matched intact flowering stalks with centimeter ruler and male/female arrows
Paired pistillate flower dissections at 20–30× showing bracteoles and stigma shape with scale
handoff: Approved Taxa Installer owns species; Diagnostic Photo Polish owns photos.
field_tip: Inspect intact spike gap, proximal sheath glands, and pistillate bracteoles together; do not force hybrid-like plants to species.
field_identification_sequence: Confirm the upper staminate and lower pistillate zones on one intact flowering stem.
Measure the bare interval between them: often 1–8 cm in T. domingensis, generally contiguous in T. latifolia. Damage or old male spikes can mislead.
Measure several fully expanded leaf blades and inspect the proximal blade and sheath for mucilage glands; use as corroboration, not a single-character diagnosis.
Dissect mature pistillate flowers at 20–30x: bracteoles present in T. domingensis, absent in T. latifolia.
For intermediate gap/width or suspected hybrids, retain Typha sp. and request reproductive diagnostic review.

diagnostic_photo_plan.photo: Fresh intact inflorescences of both species with centimeter scale and two arrows identifying zones
Matched inner sheath and first 10 cm of leaf blade, backlit macro and labeled glands
Dissected female flowers of both species at matched 20–30x with bracteole arrows and scale
Several mature leaves per species measured at same distance from sheath
Intermediate intact spike plus paired flower dissection; label uncertain rather than assigning species
